paragraphs: I'm applying for the Summer 2027 Information Security Internship in Redondo Beach. A security program that supports spacecraft manufacturing, under ITAR, NIST 800-171 and CMMC, is the kind of high-stakes environment I want to learn in. I like that interns work on real monitoring, vulnerability management and compliance tasks instead of side projects. I'm local to Irvine/Orange County, a U.S. citizen, and I finished my B.S. in Computer Science at UC Irvine with a specialization in Networked Systems.

The fundamentals you list (authentication, access control, encryption and network defense) are what I've practiced most. I built and still operate CommunicAI, an iOS app live on the App Store, and I own its security. I implemented multi-provider authentication (Sign in with Apple with nonce and SHA-256 hashing, Google OAuth, and verified email/password) and put Firebase App Check in front of every backend request. I wrote role-based access-control rules that block IDOR, privilege escalation and message spoofing, and I check them with 36 adversarial unit tests. Server-side, my Cloud Functions enforce input validation and rate limiting. In coursework and labs I've used Wireshark and Burp Suite to study MITM, ARP poisoning, DNS spoofing, SQL injection and XSS.

I haven't worked with a SIEM, EDR or vulnerability scanners yet, and that is exactly why this internship appeals to me. I'm studying for the CompTIA Security+ exam in January, and I learn fast under a heavy load. As captain of UC Irvine's NCAA Division I track and field team, I balance training, leading teammates and classes.
I'm available for the full 12-week Summer 2027 program on-site in Redondo Beach, and I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I can help your team.
